Una punta de flecha alojada en el hombro izquierdo muestra cómo murió el Hombre de Hielo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_found.en: Two hikers coming down from the Finail peak have found a body melting out of the ice in $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, on the edge of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName]. The police took it for a lost climber, but the axe beside it has a copper blade.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_found.es: Dos excursionistas que bajaban del pico Finail han encontrado un cuerpo que va quedando libre del hielo al derretirse en $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place$, en el límite de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_otzi_the_iceman').GetName]. La policía lo tomó por un alpinista perdido, pero el hacha que tiene al lado lleva una hoja de cobre.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history$

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history.en: Erika and Helmut Simon found the body on 19 September 1991, a few meters inside Italy; the first, careless recovery broke its hip with a pneumatic drill. Austria and Italy settled where the body lay, and since 1998 the Iceman has lain in a cold cell in the South Tyrol Museum of Archaeology in Bolzano. The arrowhead was found in 2001; the body carries sixty-one tattoos.
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_history.es: Erika y Helmut Simon encontraron el cuerpo el 19 de septiembre de 1991, a pocos metros dentro de Italia; la primera recuperación, descuidada, le rompió la cadera con un martillo neumático. Austria e Italia determinaron en qué país yacía el cuerpo, y desde 1998 el Hombre de Hielo reposa en una celda fría del Museo Arqueológico de Tirol del Sur, en Bolzano. La punta de flecha se halló en 2001; el cuerpo lleva sesenta y un tatuajes.

gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place.en: a hollow in the rock at the Tisenjoch pass, high in the Ötztal Alps
gm_arch_site_otzi_the_iceman_place.es: una hondonada en la roca del paso de Tisenjoch, en lo alto de los Alpes de Ötztal

gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_dug.en: On $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_palace_of_knossos').GetName], the excavators have uncovered a palace of some thirteen hundred rooms around a great court: storerooms of jars as tall as a man, light wells, staircases, a stone throne, drains and bathrooms, and walls painted with bull-leapers, lilies and dolphins. Thousands of clay tablets in two unknown scripts lie where a fire baked them hard.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history$
gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_palace_of_knossos').GetName], los excavadores han sacado a la luz un palacio de unas mil trescientas estancias en torno a un gran patio: almacenes de jarras tan altas como un hombre, pozos de luz, escaleras, un trono de piedra, desagües y baños, y muros pintados con saltadores de toros, lirios y delfines. Miles de tablillas de arcilla con dos escrituras desconocidas yacen donde un incendio las coció hasta endurecerlas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history$

gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_found.en: A merchant of Heraklion, Minos Kalokairinos, dug trial trenches on $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_palace_of_knossos').GetName], and found storerooms full of great clay jars before the Ottoman authorities stopped the work. Our scholars believe a palace older than Homer's heroes lies under the olive groves, perhaps the labyrinth of the legendary King Minos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history$
gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_found.es: Un comerciante de Heraclión, Minos Kalokairinos, abrió zanjas de prueba en $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_palace_of_knossos').GetName], y encontró almacenes llenos de grandes jarras de arcilla antes de que las autoridades otomanas detuvieran los trabajos. Nuestros eruditos creen que bajo los olivares yace un palacio más antiguo que los héroes de Homero, quizá el laberinto del legendario rey Minos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history$

gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history.en: Arthur Evans bought the site and dug it from 1900, naming the civilization Minoan after the legendary king. Evans rebuilt parts of the palace in reinforced concrete and restored frescoes from fragments, which still divides archaeologists. One of the scripts, Linear B, was deciphered by Michael Ventris in 1952 as an early form of Greek; the other, Linear A, is still unread.
gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_history.es: Arthur Evans compró el terreno y lo excavó desde 1900, y llamó minoica a la civilización por el legendario rey. Evans reconstruyó partes del palacio en hormigón armado y restauró frescos a partir de fragmentos, lo que aún divide a los arqueólogos. Una de las escrituras, el lineal B, fue descifrada por Michael Ventris en 1952 como una forma temprana del griego; la otra, el lineal A, sigue sin leerse.

gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place.en: the hill of Kephala, south of Heraklion
gm_arch_site_palace_of_knossos_place.es: la colina de Kefala, al sur de Heraclión

gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_dug.en: The excavators have pulled down the Byzantine walls on $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pergamon_altar').GetName], which were built of the altar's own stones, and gathered the frieze of the Great Altar: more than a hundred meters of high relief in which the Olympian gods fight the giants, snake-legged and winged, carved about 170 BC. The altar's foundations still stand on their terrace.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history$
gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_dug.es: Los excavadores han derribado las murallas bizantinas que había en $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pergamon_altar').GetName], construidas con las propias piedras del altar, y han reunido el friso del Gran Altar: más de cien metros de altorrelieve en el que los dioses olímpicos combaten contra los gigantes, con patas de serpiente y alados, tallado hacia 170 a. C. Los cimientos del altar siguen en pie sobre su terraza.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history$

gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_found.en: For generations lime-burners have broken the marble of $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pergamon_altar').GetName], into their kilns. Our scholars have seen fragments of reliefs built into the old Byzantine walls on the hill, and believe a great altar of the Attalid kings lies under it.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history$
gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_found.es: Desde hace generaciones los caleros rompen el mármol de $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pergamon_altar').GetName], para sus hornos. Nuestros eruditos han visto fragmentos de relieves incrustados en las viejas murallas bizantinas de la colina, y creen que bajo ella yace un gran altar de los reyes atálidas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history$

gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history.en: Carl Humann, a German engineer building roads for the Ottoman government, saw the lime kilns in the 1860s and dug the altar for the Berlin Museums from 1878 to 1886; by agreement with the Ottoman government, the frieze went to Berlin. The altar was rebuilt in the Pergamon Museum, opened in 1930. The Soviet Union took it in 1945 and returned it in 1958.
gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_history.es: Carl Humann, un ingeniero alemán que construía carreteras para el gobierno otomano, vio los hornos de cal en la década de 1860 y excavó el altar para los Museos de Berlín de 1878 a 1886; por acuerdo con el gobierno otomano, el friso fue a Berlín. El altar se reconstruyó en el Museo de Pérgamo, inaugurado en 1930. La Unión Soviética se lo llevó en 1945 y lo devolvió en 1958.

gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place.en: the acropolis of Pergamon, above the town of Bergama
gm_arch_site_pergamon_altar_place.es: la acrópolis de Pérgamo, sobre la ciudad de Bergama

gm_arch_site_pompeii_dug.en: The excavators have cleared the streets of $gm_arch_site_pompeii_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pompeii').GetName], to the walls: the forum and the basilica, temples, two theaters and an amphitheater, bakeries with loaves still in the ovens, taverns and fulleries, and the painted houses of the rich, the Villa of the Mysteries among them, with the Alexander Mosaic in the House of the Faun. Hollows in the ash, filled with plaster, give back the shapes of the people who died there.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pompeii_history$
gm_arch_site_pompeii_dug.es: Los excavadores han despejado las calles de $gm_arch_site_pompeii_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pompeii').GetName], hasta las murallas: el foro y la basílica, templos, dos teatros y un anfiteatro, panaderías con hogazas aún en los hornos, tabernas y lavanderías, y las casas pintadas de los ricos, entre ellas la Villa de los Misterios, con el Mosaico de Alejandro en la Casa del Fauno. Los huecos en la ceniza, rellenados con yeso, devuelven las formas de las personas que murieron allí.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pompeii_history$

gm_arch_site_pompeii_found.en: Royal excavators have been clearing $gm_arch_site_pompeii_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pompeii').GetName], for generations, lifting frescoes, bronzes and mosaics for the museum at Naples. The work has stopped, and a third of the town or more still lies under the ash, its streets running on beneath the vineyards.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pompeii_history$
gm_arch_site_pompeii_found.es: Excavadores reales llevan generaciones despejando $gm_arch_site_pompeii_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_pompeii').GetName], y han retirado frescos, bronces y mosaicos para el museo de Nápoles. Los trabajos se han detenido, y un tercio de la ciudad o más sigue bajo la ceniza, con sus calles prolongándose bajo los viñedos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_pompeii_history$

gm_arch_site_pompeii_history.en: Bourbon engineers began digging Pompeii in 1748, more for treasure than knowledge, and the Alexander Mosaic came out of the House of the Faun in 1831. Giuseppe Fiorelli, director from 1863, dug house by house, recorded what came out of each, and poured plaster into the hollows the bodies had left. About a third of the town is still unexcavated, and the dig goes on today.
gm_arch_site_pompeii_history.es: Los ingenieros borbónicos empezaron a excavar Pompeya en 1748, más por el tesoro que por el conocimiento, y el Mosaico de Alejandro salió de la Casa del Fauno en 1831. Giuseppe Fiorelli, director desde 1863, excavó casa por casa, registró lo que salía de cada una y vertió yeso en los huecos que habían dejado los cuerpos. Alrededor de un tercio de la ciudad sigue sin excavar, y la excavación continúa hoy.

gm_arch_site_pompeii_place.en: the ash-buried Roman town at the foot of Vesuvius, by the mouth of the Sarno
gm_arch_site_pompeii_place.es: la ciudad romana sepultada por la ceniza al pie del Vesubio, junto a la desembocadura del Sarno

gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_dug.en: Beside the ziggurat of $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_cemetery_at_ur').GetName], the excavators have opened some eighteen hundred graves, sixteen of them royal: stone tombs with rows of attendants who died to follow their masters, with gold helmets and daggers, lyres inlaid with shell and lapis lazuli, Queen Puabi's golden headdress, the goat called the Ram in a Thicket, and the Standard of Ur, whose panels show war and peace in shell and lapis.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_history$
gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_dug.es: Junto al zigurat de $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_cemetery_at_ur').GetName], los excavadores han abierto unas mil ochocientas tumbas, dieciséis de ellas reales: tumbas de piedra con hileras de sirvientes que murieron para seguir a sus amos, con yelmos y dagas de oro, liras con incrustaciones de concha y lapislázuli, el tocado de oro de la reina Puabi, la cabra llamada el Carnero en el Matorral y el Estandarte de Ur, cuyos paneles muestran la guerra y la paz en concha y lapislázuli.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_history$

gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_found.en: The bricks of $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_cemetery_at_ur').GetName], are stamped with the name of Ur, the city of Abraham in the Bible. Trial trenches beside the ziggurat have turned up gold beads in the rubbish, and our scholars believe the early kings of Sumer are buried there.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_history$
gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_found.es: Los ladrillos de $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_cemetery_at_ur').GetName], llevan estampado el nombre de Ur, la ciudad de Abraham en la Biblia. Las zanjas de prueba junto al zigurat han sacado cuentas de oro entre los desechos, y nuestros eruditos creen que allí están enterrados los primeros reyes de Sumer.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_history$

gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_histor.en: Leonard Woolley dug Ur for the British Museum and the University of Pennsylvania from 1922 to 1934, and opened the royal tombs from 1926. The finds were divided three ways, between Baghdad, London and Philadelphia. A deep flood layer under the city made Woolley famous as the finder of Noah's Flood.
gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_histor.es: Leonard Woolley excavó Ur para el Museo Británico y la Universidad de Pensilvania de 1922 a 1934, y abrió las tumbas reales desde 1926. Los hallazgos se repartieron en tres partes, entre Bagdad, Londres y Filadelfia. Una profunda capa de inundación bajo la ciudad hizo famoso a Woolley como descubridor del Diluvio de Noé.

gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place.en: Tell al-Muqayyar, the mound of Ur, near Nasiriyah
gm_arch_site_royal_cemetery_at_ur_place.es: Tell al-Muqayyar, el montículo de Ur, cerca de Nasiriya

gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_dug.en: Inside $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_tombs_of_sipan').GetName], below the looters' tunnels, the excavators have found the unrobbed tombs of the Moche lords. A warrior-priest of about AD 250 lay in a plank coffin among attendants and guards, one with the feet cut off, with a dog and llamas, wearing gold and silver masks, a crescent headdress, a necklace of gold and silver peanuts, and ear ornaments of gold and turquoise showing tiny warriors.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_history$
gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_dug.es: Dentro de $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_tombs_of_sipan').GetName], bajo los túneles de los saqueadores, los excavadores han hallado las tumbas sin saquear de los señores moche. Un sacerdote guerrero de hacia el año 250 d. C. yacía en un ataúd de tablas entre sirvientes y guardias, uno de ellos con los pies cortados, con un perro y llamas, con máscaras de oro y plata, un tocado en forma de media luna, un collar de cacahuetes de oro y plata y adornos de orejas de oro y turquesa con diminutos guerreros.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_history$

gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_found.en: Gold ornaments finer than any the dealers have seen are being sold in the towns of the north coast, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_tombs_of_sipan').GetName], and the police have traced them to looters tunneling into $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place$. One looter has been killed in a raid, and the villagers say the mound is theirs to dig.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_history$
gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_found.es: En los pueblos de la costa norte, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_royal_tombs_of_sipan').GetName], se venden adornos de oro más finos que cualquiera que hayan visto los comerciantes, y la policía los ha seguido hasta unos saqueadores que cavan túneles en $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place$. Un saqueador ha muerto en una redada, y los aldeanos dicen que el túmulo es suyo para excavarlo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_history$

gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_histor.en: Looters broke into a tomb in 1987, and Walter Alva of the Brüning Museum stepped in under police guard. The tomb of the Lord of Sipán, found that year, was the richest unlooted tomb then found in the Americas, and others followed, among them the Old Lord of Sipán. The finds are in the Royal Tombs of Sipán Museum in Lambayeque.
gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_histor.es: Unos saqueadores irrumpieron en una tumba en 1987, y Walter Alva, del Museo Brüning, intervino bajo custodia policial. La tumba del Señor de Sipán, hallada ese año, fue la tumba intacta más rica encontrada hasta entonces en América, y siguieron otras, entre ellas la del Viejo Señor de Sipán. Los hallazgos están en el Museo Tumbas Reales de Sipán, en Lambayeque.

gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place.en: Huaca Rajada, the eroded adobe pyramids at Sipán
gm_arch_site_royal_tombs_of_sipan_place.es: Huaca Rajada, las pirámides de adobe erosionadas de Sipán

gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_dug.en: Two pits in $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sanxingdui_pits').GetName], hold the offerings of a kingdom no chronicle names: bronze heads and masks with bulging eyes and great ears, some covered in gold leaf, a bronze figure taller than a man, a bronze tree four meters high hung with birds, and dozens of elephant tusks, all deliberately broken and burned about 1200 BC.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history$
gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_dug.es: Dos fosas en $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sanxingdui_pits').GetName], contienen las ofrendas de un reino que ninguna crónica nombra: cabezas y máscaras de bronce de ojos saltones y grandes orejas, algunas cubiertas de pan de oro, una figura de bronce más alta que un hombre, un árbol de bronce de cuatro metros de altura con pájaros colgados, y decenas de colmillos de elefante, todo ello deliberadamente roto y quemado hacia 1200 a. C.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history$

gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_found.en: A farmer cutting an irrigation ditch in $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sanxingdui_pits').GetName], has struck a cache of jade and stone: discs, blades and rings of a kind nobody in the province has seen. Collectors in Chengdu are already buying them.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history$
gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_found.es: Un agricultor que abría una acequia de riego en $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sanxingdui_pits').GetName], ha topado con un escondrijo de jade y piedra: discos, hojas y anillos de un tipo que nadie en la provincia ha visto. Los coleccionistas de Chengdu ya los están comprando.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history$

gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history.en: Yan Daocheng, a farmer, found a jade cache in 1929; the two great sacrificial pits were found by brickworks laborers in 1986. They belong to the Shu culture of the Sichuan basin, independent of the Shang dynasty of the north. Six more pits, opened from 2020, have yielded more gold masks. The finds are in the Sanxingdui Museum.
gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_history.es: Yan Daocheng, un agricultor, encontró un escondrijo de jade en 1929; las dos grandes fosas sacrificiales fueron halladas por obreros de una fábrica de ladrillos en 1986. Pertenecen a la cultura Shu de la cuenca de Sichuan, independiente de la dinastía Shang del norte. Seis fosas más, abiertas desde 2020, han dado más máscaras de oro. Los hallazgos están en el Museo de Sanxingdui.

gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place.en: the fields beside the Mamuhe river at Sanxingdui, near Guanghan
gm_arch_site_sanxingdui_pits_place.es: los campos junto al río Mamuhe en Sanxingdui, cerca de Guanghan

gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_dug.en: In the shafts and chambers of $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sidon_necropolis').GetName], the excavators have found the sarcophagi of the kings of Sidon: Egyptian-style coffins of dark stone, one inscribed for King Eshmunazar II, and marble ones carved by Greek sculptors, the finest showing Alexander the Great at war and at the hunt, its paint still on the stone.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history$
gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_dug.es: En los pozos y cámaras de $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sidon_necropolis').GetName], los excavadores han hallado los sarcófagos de los reyes de Sidón: ataúdes de piedra oscura de estilo egipcio, uno inscrito para el rey Eshmunazar II, y otros de mármol tallados por escultores griegos, el más fino de los cuales muestra a Alejandro Magno en la guerra y en la caza, con la pintura aún sobre la piedra.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history$

gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_found.en: Quarrymen in $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sidon_necropolis').GetName], keep breaking into chambers holding stone coffins, and a black sarcophagus with a long Phoenician inscription has come out of one. Our scholars believe the kings of Sidon are buried there.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history$
gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_found.es: Unos canteros que trabajan en $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sidon_necropolis').GetName], siguen dando con cámaras que contienen ataúdes de piedra, y de una de ellas ha salido un sarcófago negro con una larga inscripción fenicia. Nuestros eruditos creen que allí están enterrados los reyes de Sidón.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history$

gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history.en: The sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II was found in 1855 and went to the Louvre, and Ernest Renan's mission dug at Sidon in 1860 and 1861. In 1887 Osman Hamdi Bey, the Ottoman archaeologist, excavated the royal necropolis and brought the Alexander Sarcophagus to Istanbul, where the Imperial Museum, now the Istanbul Archaeology Museums, was built to house it.
gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_history.es: El sarcófago de Eshmunazar II se halló en 1855 y fue al Louvre, y la misión de Ernest Renan excavó en Sidón en 1860 y 1861. En 1887 Osman Hamdi Bey, el arqueólogo otomano, excavó la necrópolis real y llevó el Sarcófago de Alejandro a Estambul, donde se construyó para albergarlo el Museo Imperial, hoy Museos Arqueológicos de Estambul.

gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place.en: the rock-cut burial grounds in the orchards around Sidon
gm_arch_site_sidon_necropolis_place.es: las necrópolis excavadas en la roca entre los huertos que rodean Sidón

gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_dug.en: In the great mound among $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sutton_hoo').GetName], the outline of a ship twenty-seven meters long lies traced in rivets in the sand, the wood long rotted away. In its burial chamber lay the treasure of an Anglo-Saxon king: a crested iron helmet with a face mask, a great gold buckle, shoulder clasps of gold and garnet, a purse lid, silver bowls from Byzantium, a sword, a shield and a whetstone scepter.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history$
gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_dug.es: En el gran túmulo situado entre $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sutton_hoo').GetName], el contorno de un barco de veintisiete metros de eslora aparece trazado con remaches en la arena, con la madera pudrida hace mucho. En su cámara funeraria yacía el tesoro de un rey anglosajón: un yelmo de hierro con cresta y máscara facial, una gran hebilla de oro, broches de hombro de oro y granate, la tapa de una bolsa, cuencos de plata de Bizancio, una espada, un escudo y un cetro de piedra de afilar.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history$

gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_found.en: The owner of the Sutton Hoo estate, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sutton_hoo').GetName], curious about the old mounds on the estate, has hired a local excavator to open them. In the largest of $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place$ the excavator has found rows of iron rivets in the sand where the timbers of a ship once lay.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history$
gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_found.es: El propietario de la finca de Sutton Hoo, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_sutton_hoo').GetName], curioso por los viejos túmulos de la finca, ha contratado a un excavador local para abrirlos. En el mayor de $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place$ el excavador ha encontrado hileras de remaches de hierro en la arena, donde antes yacían los maderos de un barco.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history$

gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history.en: Edith Pretty, the landowner, hired Basil Brown, who found the ship in 1939; Charles Phillips's team cleared the chamber weeks before the Second World War began. The grave is probably that of King Rædwald of East Anglia, who died about 624. An inquest ruled the treasure Mrs Pretty's, and Mrs Pretty gave it to the British Museum.
gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_history.es: Edith Pretty, la propietaria de las tierras, contrató a Basil Brown, que encontró el barco en 1939; el equipo de Charles Phillips despejó la cámara pocas semanas antes del comienzo de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. La tumba es probablemente la del rey Rædwald de Anglia Oriental, que murió hacia 624. Una investigación judicial declaró el tesoro propiedad de la señora Pretty, y la señora Pretty lo donó al Museo Británico.

gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place.en: the burial mounds of the Sutton Hoo estate, above the river Deben near Woodbridge
gm_arch_site_sutton_hoo_place.es: los túmulos funerarios de la finca de Sutton Hoo, sobre el río Deben, cerca de Woodbridge

gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_dug.en: The excavators have stripped the earth from the Pyramid of the Sun in $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_teotihuacan').GetName], rebuilt its stepped terraces, and cleared the Avenue of the Dead between it and the Pyramid of the Moon. At the avenue's far end they found a great walled court and a temple faced with carved serpent heads, the Feathered Serpent among them, still painted.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history$
gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_dug.es: Los excavadores han retirado la tierra de la Pirámide del Sol en $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_teotihuacan').GetName], han reconstruido sus terrazas escalonadas y han despejado la Calzada de los Muertos entre ella y la Pirámide de la Luna. Al final de la calzada hallaron un gran patio amurallado y un templo revestido de cabezas de serpiente talladas, entre ellas las de la Serpiente Emplumada, todavía pintadas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history$

gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_found.en: Two great mounds rise from the fields of $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_teotihuacan').GetName]. The Aztecs called them the Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon, and the place the city of the gods. Our scholars hold that they are true pyramids buried in their own rubble, along an avenue of lesser mounds.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history$
gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_found.es: Dos grandes montículos emergen de los campos que se extienden en $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_teotihuacan').GetName]. Los aztecas los llamaron las Pirámides del Sol y de la Luna, y al lugar, la ciudad de los dioses. Nuestros eruditos sostienen que son auténticas pirámides enterradas en sus propios escombros, a lo largo de una calzada de montículos menores.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history$

gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history.en: Leopoldo Batres restored the Pyramid of the Sun for the centenary of independence in 1910, cutting away several meters of its outer face. Manuel Gamio dug the Temple of the Feathered Serpent from 1917; the city is now thought to have burned around 550.
gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_history.es: Leopoldo Batres restauró la Pirámide del Sol para el centenario de la independencia en 1910, cortando varios metros de su cara exterior. Manuel Gamio excavó el Templo de la Serpiente Emplumada desde 1917; ahora se cree que la ciudad ardió hacia el año 550.

gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place.en: the valley of San Juan Teotihuacan, northeast of the capital
gm_arch_site_teotihuacan_place.es: el valle de San Juan Teotihuacán, al noreste de la capital

gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_dug.en: In pits in $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_terracotta_army').GetName], the excavators have laid bare an army in battle order: thousands of life-sized warriors of fired clay, each face different, archers, infantry and generals, with horses, wooden chariots and real bronze weapons still sharp, made to guard the tomb of Qin Shi Huang, who unified China and died in 210 BC.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history$
gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_dug.es: En fosas situadas en $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_terracotta_army').GetName], los excavadores han dejado al descubierto un ejército en orden de batalla: miles de guerreros de arcilla cocida de tamaño natural, cada uno con un rostro distinto, arqueros, infantería y generales, con caballos, carros de madera y armas de bronce auténticas aún afiladas, hechos para custodiar la tumba de Qin Shi Huang, que unificó China y murió en 210 a. C.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history$

gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_found.en: Farmers digging a well during a drought in $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_terracotta_army').GetName], have brought up pieces of fired clay: a head with a topknot, an arm, bronze arrowheads. A local museum worker has bought the fragments and fitted them together into a life-sized soldier.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history$
gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_found.es: Unos agricultores que cavaban un pozo durante una sequía en $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_terracotta_army').GetName], han sacado trozos de arcilla cocida: una cabeza con moño, un brazo, puntas de flecha de bronce. Un empleado del museo local ha comprado los fragmentos y los ha encajado hasta formar un soldado de tamaño natural.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history$

gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history.en: Yang Zhifa and neighbors struck the first pit in March 1974, and Zhao Kangmin, a local museum worker, recognized the pieces. Three pits have yielded some two thousand figures of an estimated eight thousand. The emperor's own mound, which the historian Sima Qian said held rivers of mercury, has never been opened.
gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_history.es: Yang Zhifa y sus vecinos dieron con la primera fosa en marzo de 1974, y Zhao Kangmin, empleado del museo local, reconoció las piezas. Tres fosas han dado unas dos mil figuras de las ocho mil estimadas. El túmulo del propio emperador, que según el historiador Sima Qian contenía ríos de mercurio, nunca se ha abierto.

gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place.en: the fields east of the burial mound of the First Emperor of Qin, near Lintong
gm_arch_site_terracotta_army_place.es: los campos al este del túmulo funerario del Primer Emperador de Qin, cerca de Lintong

gm_arch_site_tikal_dug.en: Cutting through the forest of $gm_arch_site_tikal_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tikal').GetName], the expedition has cleared the Great Plaza of a Maya city. Two temple pyramids face each other across it, the tallest of the temples crowned by a roof comb some seventy meters above the ground, with carved stelae of its kings, palaces and ball courts around it and causeways leading off into the forest to other temples.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tikal_history$
gm_arch_site_tikal_dug.es: Abriéndose paso por $gm_arch_site_tikal_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tikal').GetName], la expedición ha despejado la Gran Plaza de una ciudad maya. Dos pirámides-templo se enfrentan a ambos lados de ella, la más alta de los templos coronada por una crestería a unos setenta metros sobre el suelo, con estelas talladas de sus reyes, palacios y canchas de pelota a su alrededor y calzadas que se internan en la selva hacia otros templos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tikal_history$

gm_arch_site_tikal_found.en: Chicle gatherers and the governor's men in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tikal').GetName] speak of stone temples standing above the trees of $gm_arch_site_tikal_place$, nameless and abandoned. Our scholars have read their reports and believe they mark a city of the ancient Maya greater than any yet known.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tikal_history$
gm_arch_site_tikal_found.es: Los recolectores de chicle y los hombres del gobernador en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tikal').GetName] hablan de templos de piedra que se alzan por encima de los árboles de $gm_arch_site_tikal_place$, anónimos y abandonados. Nuestros eruditos han leído sus informes y creen que señalan una ciudad de los antiguos mayas mayor que cualquiera conocida hasta ahora.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tikal_history$

gm_arch_site_tikal_history.en: Modesto Méndez, governor of Petén, and Ambrosio Tut reached the ruins in 1848 and published the first account. Alfred Maudslay photographed them in the 1880s, and the University of Pennsylvania excavated from 1956 to 1970; its glyphs have since been read to name the city's kings and its wars with Calakmul.
gm_arch_site_tikal_history.es: Modesto Méndez, gobernador de Petén, y Ambrosio Tut llegaron a las ruinas en 1848 y publicaron el primer relato. Alfred Maudslay las fotografió en la década de 1880, y la Universidad de Pensilvania excavó de 1956 a 1970; desde entonces se han descifrado sus glifos, que nombran a los reyes de la ciudad y sus guerras con Calakmul.

gm_arch_site_tikal_place.en: the forest of Petén, north of Lake Petén Itzá
gm_arch_site_tikal_place.es: la selva de Petén, al norte del lago Petén Itzá

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_dug.en: Beneath $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_alexander').GetName], the excavators have broken into a vaulted tomb of alabaster and marble, its walls painted, its corridors lined with the burials of later Ptolemies, and in its central chamber an empty pedestal and the fragments of a coffin of glass, which the Ptolemies put in place of the golden one: the tomb, the scholars are sure, of Alexander the Great.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_alexander').GetName], los excavadores han irrumpido en una tumba abovedada de alabastro y mármol, con las paredes pintadas y los corredores flanqueados por los enterramientos de Ptolomeos posteriores, y en su cámara central un pedestal vacío y los fragmentos de un ataúd de cristal, que los Ptolomeos pusieron en lugar del de oro: la tumba, están seguros los eruditos, de Alejandro Magno.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_found.en: Ancient writers say the Ptolemies laid Alexander the Great in a mausoleum, the Soma, at the crossroads of their capital. Our archaeologists, mapping with ground radar under $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_alexander').GetName], have found a great vaulted hollow where the old streets crossed.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_found.es: Los escritores antiguos dicen que los Ptolomeos depositaron a Alejandro Magno en un mausoleo, el Soma, en el cruce de caminos de su capital. Nuestros arqueólogos, que cartografían con georradar bajo $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_alexander').GetName], han encontrado una gran cavidad abovedada donde se cruzaban las viejas calles.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history.en: Alexander died in Babylon in 323 BC. Ptolemy I diverted the body to Egypt, and it lay in Alexandria, visited by Julius Caesar and Augustus, until the tomb drops out of the record in the late fourth century AD. More than a hundred and forty official searches have failed to find it. This find is speculative: the tomb has never been located.
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_history.es: Alejandro murió en Babilonia en 323 a. C. Ptolomeo I desvió el cuerpo a Egipto, y yació en Alejandría, visitado por Julio César y Augusto, hasta que la tumba desaparece de los registros a finales del siglo IV d. C. Más de ciento cuarenta búsquedas oficiales no han logrado encontrarla. Este hallazgo es especulativo: la tumba nunca ha sido localizada.

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place.en: the old royal quarter of Alexandria, near the Nabi Daniel mosque
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_alexander_place.es: el antiguo barrio real de Alejandría, cerca de la mezquita de Nabi Daniel

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_dug.en: Under $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_marquis_yi').GetName], the excavators have pumped the water out of a wooden tomb of four chambers, sealed about 433 BC for Yi, Marquis of Zeng: the marquis's nested lacquered coffins, the coffins of twenty-one young women, weapons, chariot fittings, bronze vessels, and a set of sixty-five bronze bells still hanging on their lacquered rack, each bell sounding two notes.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_marquis_yi').GetName], los excavadores han bombeado el agua de una tumba de madera de cuatro cámaras, sellada hacia 433 a. C. para Yi, marqués de Zeng: los ataúdes lacados encajados del marqués, los ataúdes de veintiuna jóvenes, armas, piezas de carro, vasijas de bronce y un juego de sesenta y cinco campanas de bronce que aún cuelgan de su bastidor lacado, cada campana con dos notas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_found.en: An army unit leveling $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_marquis_yi').GetName], for a factory has blasted into reddish-brown earth unlike the rock around it, and stopped. The experts of the provincial museum say it is the fill of a great tomb.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_found.es: Una unidad del ejército que allanaba $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_marquis_yi').GetName], para levantar una fábrica ha dado con explosivos en una tierra de color marrón rojizo, distinta de la roca circundante, y se ha detenido. Los expertos del museo provincial dicen que es el relleno de una gran tumba.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history.en: A People's Liberation Army unit found the tomb in 1977, and it was dug in 1978 under Tan Weisi of the Hubei Provincial Museum. The bells, inscribed with the names of the notes they sound, showed that musicians of the fifth century BC tuned to a twelve-note scale. They are in the Hubei Provincial Museum in Wuhan.
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_history.es: Una unidad del Ejército Popular de Liberación halló la tumba en 1977, y se excavó en 1978 bajo la dirección de Tan Weisi, del Museo Provincial de Hubei. Las campanas, con inscripciones de los nombres de las notas que emiten, demostraron que los músicos del siglo V a. C. afinaban según una escala de doce notas. Se conservan en el Museo Provincial de Hubei, en Wuhan.

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_marquis_yi_place.es: la colina de Leigudun, a las afueras de Suizhou

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_dug.en: Under the floor of $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_pakal').GetName], the excavators have cleared a stair choked with rubble, down past the bones of sacrificed attendants, to a vaulted crypt at ground level. In a great stone sarcophagus under a carved lid lay a king in a mask of jade mosaic, with jade collars, rings and ear spools: K'inich Janaab' Pakal, who ruled Palenque for sixty-eight years and died in 683.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_pakal').GetName], los excavadores han despejado, bajo el suelo, una escalera atascada de escombros que desciende, pasando junto a los huesos de los asistentes sacrificados, hasta una cripta abovedada a nivel del suelo. En un gran sarcófago de piedra, bajo una tapa tallada, yacía un rey con una máscara de mosaico de jade, con collares, anillos y orejeras de jade: K'inich Janaab' Pakal, que gobernó Palenque durante sesenta y ocho años y murió en 683.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_found.en: Our archaeologists have noticed that one floor slab in $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_pakal').GetName], has holes for lifting, and that the temple's walls run on below the floor. They believe a stair, filled with rubble by the Maya themselves, leads down into the pyramid.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_found.es: Nuestros arqueólogos han advertido que, en $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_pakal').GetName], una losa del suelo tiene agujeros para levantarla y que los muros del templo siguen por debajo del suelo. Creen que una escalera, rellenada de escombros por los propios mayas, desciende hacia el interior de la pirámide.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history.en: Alberto Ruz Lhuillier lifted the slab in 1948 and spent four seasons clearing the stair before reaching the crypt on 15 June 1952, overturning the belief that Maya pyramids were never tombs. The jade mask was stolen from the National Museum of Anthropology in Mexico City in 1985 and recovered in 1989.
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_history.es: Alberto Ruz Lhuillier levantó la losa en 1948 y dedicó cuatro temporadas a despejar la escalera antes de llegar a la cripta el 15 de junio de 1952, lo que desmintió la creencia de que las pirámides mayas nunca fueron tumbas. La máscara de jade fue robada del Museo Nacional de Antropología de Ciudad de México en 1985 y recuperada en 1989.

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place.en: the Temple of the Inscriptions, the tallest pyramid at Palenque
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_pakal_place.es: el Templo de las Inscripciones, la pirámide más alta de Palenque

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_dug.en: Under $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_philip_ii').GetName], the excavators have found royal tombs, two of them unrobbed: a vaulted tomb with a painted hunting frieze on its facade, and inside it a marble sarcophagus holding a gold chest stamped with a sixteen-rayed star, the burned bones of a man wrapped in purple and gold, a gold oak wreath, armor and small ivory portrait heads; in the antechamber, a second gold chest held a woman's bones.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_philip_ii').GetName], los excavadores han encontrado tumbas reales, dos de ellas sin saquear: una tumba abovedada con un friso de caza pintado en su fachada y, dentro, un sarcófago de mármol con un cofre de oro marcado con una estrella de dieciséis rayos, los huesos quemados de un hombre envuelto en púrpura y oro, una corona de roble de oro, armadura y pequeñas cabezas de marfil con retratos; en la antecámara, un segundo cofre de oro contenía los huesos de una mujer.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_found.en: Our archaeologists believe the village of Vergina, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_philip_ii').GetName], stands on Aigai, the first capital of the Macedonian kings and the place where they were buried. Probes into $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_place$, a mound of earth twelve meters high and more than a hundred across, have struck the fill of tombs.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_found.es: Nuestros arqueólogos creen que el pueblo de Vergina, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_philip_ii').GetName], se alza sobre Egas, la primera capital de los reyes macedonios y el lugar donde fueron enterrados. Los sondeos en $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_place$, un montículo de tierra de doce metros de altura y más de cien de anchura, han dado con el relleno de unas tumbas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history.en: Manolis Andronikos opened the tombs in November 1977. Andronikos held Tomb II to be that of Philip II of Macedon, Alexander the Great's father, murdered in 336 BC; some scholars argue it is Philip III Arrhidaeus's instead. The finds stay at Vergina, in a museum built inside the mound itself.
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_philip_ii_history.es: Manolis Andronikos abrió las tumbas en noviembre de 1977. Andronikos sostuvo que la Tumba II era la de Filipo II de Macedonia, padre de Alejandro Magno, asesinado en 336 a. C.; algunos estudiosos sostienen que es más bien la de Filipo III Arrideo. Los hallazgos permanecen en Vergina, en un museo construido dentro del propio túmulo.

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_dug.en: Below the entrance to the tomb of Ramesses VI, on $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place$ in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_tutankhamun').GetName], sixteen steps lead down to a sealed door. Beyond it lie four crowded rooms the robbers barely touched: gilded shrines nested one inside the other, chariots, couches, statues, chests and jewelry, some five thousand objects, and in a stone sarcophagus three coffins, the innermost of solid gold, around the mummy of Tutankhamun in a mask of gold.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_dug.es: Bajo la entrada a la tumba de Ramsés VI, en $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_tutankhamun').GetName], dieciséis escalones descienden hasta una puerta sellada. Tras ella hay cuatro estancias abarrotadas que los ladrones apenas tocaron: santuarios dorados encajados unos dentro de otros, carros, lechos, estatuas, cofres y joyas, unos cinco mil objetos, y en un sarcófago de piedra tres ataúdes, el más interior de oro macizo, alrededor de la momia de Tutankamón con una máscara de oro.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_found.en: Every royal tomb found at Thebes was robbed in antiquity, and most scholars say the valley of the royal tombs has given up all it had. Our Egyptologists disagree: objects bearing the name of an obscure boy king, Tutankhamun, have turned up nearby, and they believe the boy king's tomb lies somewhere under the rubble of $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_tutankhamun').GetName].\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history$
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_found.es: Todas las tumbas reales encontradas en Tebas fueron saqueadas en la Antigüedad, y la mayoría de los estudiosos dicen que el valle de las tumbas reales ya ha dado todo lo que tenía. Nuestros egiptólogos discrepan: han aparecido cerca objetos con el nombre de un oscuro rey niño, Tutankamón, y creen que la tumba del rey niño yace en algún lugar bajo los escombros, en $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_tomb_of_tutankhamun').GetName].\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history$

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history.en: Howard Carter, paid by Lord Carnarvon, found the steps on 4 November 1922; asked what could be seen through the first hole, Carter answered 'Wonderful things.' Clearing the tomb took ten years. Egypt kept every object, refusing the customary division of finds; they are in the Grand Egyptian Museum, while the mummy still lies in the tomb.
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_history.es: Howard Carter, financiado por lord Carnarvon, encontró los escalones el 4 de noviembre de 1922; al preguntarle qué se veía por el primer agujero, Carter respondió: «Cosas maravillosas». Despejar la tumba llevó diez años. Egipto se quedó con todos los objetos y rechazó el reparto habitual de los hallazgos; están en el Gran Museo Egipcio, mientras que la momia sigue en la tumba.

gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place.en: the floor of the Valley of the Kings, on the west bank at Thebes
gm_arch_site_tomb_of_tutankhamun_place.es: el fondo del Valle de los Reyes, en la orilla occidental de Tebas

gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_dug.en: The excavators have cut down through $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_troy_hisarlik').GetName], and found not one city but nine, each built on the ruins of the last: walls, gates and ramps, burned levels and rebuilt ones. Near the walls of the second city lay a hoard of gold and silver, diadems of thousands of gold leaves, earrings, cups and bracelets, which the diggers call Priam's Treasure.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history$
gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_dug.es: En $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_troy_hisarlik').GetName], los excavadores han cavado hacia abajo y han encontrado no una ciudad sino nueve, cada una construida sobre las ruinas de la anterior: murallas, puertas y rampas, niveles quemados y otros reconstruidos. Cerca de las murallas de la segunda ciudad había un tesoro de oro y plata, con diademas de miles de hojas de oro, pendientes, copas y brazaletes, al que los excavadores llaman el Tesoro de Príamo.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history$

gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_found.en: Our scholars have set Homer beside the map. Against those who look for Troy at Pınarbaşı, they place it under $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_troy_hisarlik').GetName]: a hill of rubble and ash where the farmer of part of the hill has already found ancient walls.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history$
gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_found.es: Nuestros eruditos han puesto a Homero junto al mapa. Frente a quienes buscan Troya en Pınarbaşı, la sitúan bajo $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_troy_hisarlik').GetName]: una colina de escombros y ceniza donde el agricultor propietario de parte de la colina ya ha encontrado muros antiguos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history$

gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history.en: Frank Calvert, who owned part of the hill, dug trial trenches in the 1860s. Heinrich Schliemann dug there from 1871 and found the treasure in 1873; Schliemann smuggled it to Athens and later gave it to Berlin. The Red Army carried it off in 1945, and it is in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow. The city of the Trojan War is now thought to be Troy VI or VIIa, far above the treasure's layer.
gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_history.es: Frank Calvert, que era dueño de parte de la colina, abrió zanjas de prueba en la década de 1860. Heinrich Schliemann excavó allí desde 1871 y encontró el tesoro en 1873; Schliemann lo sacó de contrabando a Atenas y más tarde lo regaló a Berlín. El Ejército Rojo se lo llevó en 1945, y se encuentra en el Museo Pushkin de Moscú. Hoy se cree que la ciudad de la guerra de Troya es Troya VI o VIIa, muy por encima del estrato del tesoro.

gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place.en: the mound of Hisarlik, above the plain of the Scamander near the Dardanelles
gm_arch_site_troy_hisarlik_place.es: el montículo de Hisarlik, sobre la llanura del Escamandro, cerca de los Dardanelos

gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_dug.en: Down through twenty meters of volcanic rock at $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_villa_of_the_papyri').GetName], the excavators have opened the villa's lower floors, buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, and found more of its library: cases of scrolls burned to charcoal, which scanners now read letter by letter. Among them, the scholars hope, are books of Greek and Latin lost for two thousand years.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history$
gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_dug.es: Tras atravesar veinte metros de roca volcánica en $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_villa_of_the_papyri').GetName], los excavadores han abierto los pisos inferiores de la villa, sepultados por el Vesubio en el 79 d. C., y han encontrado más de su biblioteca: estuches de rollos carbonizados que ahora los escáneres leen letra a letra. Entre ellos, esperan los eruditos, hay libros en griego y en latín perdidos desde hace dos mil años.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history$

gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_found.en: Eighteenth-century tunnelers found a library of carbonized scrolls in $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_villa_of_the_papyri').GetName], and gave up when the tunnels filled with gas. Our archaeologists believe the villa's lower floors were never reached, and that more of its library lies there, under twenty meters of volcanic rock.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history$
gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_found.es: En el siglo XVIII, unos tuneleros encontraron una biblioteca de rollos carbonizados en $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_villa_of_the_papyri').GetName], y desistieron cuando los túneles se llenaron de gas. Nuestros arqueólogos creen que nunca se llegó a los pisos inferiores de la villa y que allí yace más de su biblioteca, bajo veinte metros de roca volcánica.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history$

gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history.en: Karl Weber's tunnels found the villa in 1750 and about eighteen hundred scrolls, most of them works of the Epicurean philosopher Philodemus. Its lower levels were found in the 1990s but have not been dug. Since 2023, X-ray scans read by machine learning have begun to recover text from scrolls too fragile to unroll. Whether a lost library lies below is not known: this find is speculative.
gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_history.es: Los túneles de Karl Weber dieron en 1750 con la villa y con unos mil ochocientos rollos, la mayoría obras del filósofo epicúreo Filodemo. Sus niveles inferiores se localizaron en la década de 1990, pero no se han excavado. Desde 2023, los escaneos de rayos X leídos mediante aprendizaje automático han empezado a recuperar texto de rollos demasiado frágiles para desenrollarlos. No se sabe si debajo hay una biblioteca perdida: este hallazgo es especulativo.

gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place.en: the buried Roman villa outside Herculaneum
gm_arch_site_villa_of_the_papyri_place.es: la villa romana sepultada a las afueras de Herculano

gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_dug.en: Below $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_vindolanda_tablets').GetName], the dig has gone down through waterlogged layers that kept what the garrison threw away: shoes, cloth and tools, and above all more than a thousand thin wooden leaf tablets written in ink: duty rosters, accounts, requests for leave and for beer, and a birthday invitation from one officer's wife to another.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history$
gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_dug.es: Bajo $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_vindolanda_tablets').GetName], la excavación ha atravesado capas anegadas que conservaron lo que la guarnición tiró: zapatos, tela y herramientas y, sobre todo, más de mil finas tablillas de madera escritas con tinta: listas de servicio, cuentas, peticiones de permiso y de cerveza, y una invitación de cumpleaños de la esposa de un oficial a la de otro.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history$

gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_found.en: Drainage work below $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place$, in [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_vindolanda_tablets').GetName], has struck a layer of black, airless earth. The laborers have brought up leather shoes, a wooden comb, and thin slivers of wood that look, under a lens, as if they were once written on.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history$
gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_found.es: Unas obras de drenaje bajo $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place$, en [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_vindolanda_tablets').GetName], han dado con una capa de tierra negra y sin aire. Los obreros han sacado zapatos de cuero, un peine de madera y finas láminas de madera que, bajo una lupa, parecen haber tenido escritura.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history$

gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history.en: Robin Birley found the first tablets in 1973, digging the fort's ditches and drains. Written between about AD 85 and 130, they are the oldest surviving handwritten documents in Britain, and Claudia Severa's invitation to Sulpicia Lepidina is among the earliest known writing in Latin by a woman. Most are in the British Museum.
gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_history.es: Robin Birley encontró las primeras tablillas en 1973, al excavar los fosos y desagües del fuerte. Escritas entre el 85 y el 130 d. C. aproximadamente, son los documentos manuscritos más antiguos que se conservan en Britania, y la invitación de Claudia Severa a Sulpicia Lepidina es uno de los primeros textos latinos conocidos escritos por una mujer. La mayoría están en el Museo Británico.

gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place.en: the Roman fort of Vindolanda, behind Hadrian's Wall
gm_arch_site_vindolanda_tablets_place.es: el fuerte romano de Vindolanda, tras el Muro de Adriano

gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.en: On the terrace above the theater of $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_place$, off the coast of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_winged_victory_of_samothrace').GetName], the diggers have lifted a marble goddess from the earth in more than a hundred fragments: a winged Victory alighting on the prow of a warship, the robes blown back by the sea wind, carved about 190 BC. The head and arms are lost; the prow, of gray marble, lies nearby in pieces.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_history$
gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.es: En la terraza sobre el teatro, en $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_place$, frente a la costa de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_winged_victory_of_samothrace').GetName], los excavadores han sacado de la tierra una diosa de mármol en más de cien fragmentos: una Victoria alada posándose en la proa de un buque de guerra, con las vestiduras echadas hacia atrás por el viento del mar, tallada hacia el 190 a. C. Se han perdido la cabeza y los brazos; la proa, de mármol gris, yace cerca hecha pedazos.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_history$

gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.en: Travelers describe the ruins of a sanctuary of mystery cults on the north shore of Samothrace, off the coast of [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_winged_victory_of_samothrace').GetName]. Our classicists believe $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_place$ was rich in offerings, and that the hillside above its theater hides more than broken columns.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_history$
gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.es: Los viajeros describen las ruinas de un santuario de cultos mistéricos en la costa norte de Samotracia, frente a la costa de [SCOPE.sState('gm_arch_ev_winged_victory_of_samothrace').GetName]. Nuestros filólogos clásicos creen que $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_place$ era rico en ofrendas y que la ladera sobre su teatro esconde algo más que columnas rotas.\n\n$gm_arch_history_lead$ $gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrace_history$

gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.en: Charles Champoiseau, the French vice-consul at Adrianople, found the statue in April 1863 and shipped it to the Louvre, where it was first shown in 1866. The prow followed in 1879, and the reassembled Victory has stood at the head of the Daru staircase since 1884. Fragments of the right hand were found in 1950.
gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.es: Charles Champoiseau, vicecónsul francés en Adrianópolis, encontró la estatua en abril de 1863 y la envió al Louvre, donde se expuso por primera vez en 1866. La proa le siguió en 1879, y la Victoria, vuelta a montar, se alza en lo alto de la escalera Daru desde 1884. En 1950 se hallaron fragmentos de la mano derecha.

gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.en: the Sanctuary of the Great Gods on the island of Samothrace
gm_arch_site_winged_victory_of_samothrac.es: el Santuario de los Grandes Dioses, en la isla de Samotracia

gm_arch_suspend_tooltip.en:

gm_boon_centenary_desc.en: A monument to the country's founding draws its peoples together. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_centenary_desc.es: Un monumento a la fundación del país une a sus pueblos. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_defeat_desc.en: A memorial to the fallen lets the country grieve together instead of turning on its government. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_defeat_desc.es: Un monumento a los caídos permite al país llorar unido en lugar de volverse contra su gobierno. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_faith_desc.en: A great shrine to the new faith draws the doubtful in. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_faith_desc.es: Un gran santuario a la nueva fe atrae a los indecisos. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_great_power_desc.en: A monument marks the country's rise among the great powers, and the world takes note. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_great_power_desc.es: Un monumento marca el ascenso del país entre las grandes potencias, y el mundo toma nota. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_homecoming_desc.en: A monument carried off as a trophy stands in its own city again.
gm_boon_homecoming_desc.es: Un monumento arrebatado como trofeo vuelve a alzarse en su propia ciudad.

gm_boon_regime_desc.en: A monument proclaims the new order, and those who welcome it are louder for a time. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_regime_desc.es: Un monumento proclama el nuevo orden, y quienes lo reciben con agrado alzan más la voz durante un tiempo. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_reign_desc.en: A monument marks the start of the reign, and the new ruler's word carries further for a time. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_reign_desc.es: Un monumento marca el inicio del reinado, y la palabra del nuevo gobernante llega más lejos durante un tiempo. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_ruler_death_desc.en: A mausoleum for the late ruler lends the government the dignity of their memory. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_ruler_death_desc.es: Un mausoleo para el difunto gobernante presta al gobierno la dignidad de su memoria. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_space_desc.en: A monument to the country's first in space fires a generation of engineers and scientists. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_space_desc.es: Un monumento al primer logro del país en el espacio enardece a una generación de ingenieros y científicos. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_tech_artistic.en: A Golden Age of the Arts
gm_boon_tech_artistic.es: Una edad de oro de las artes

gm_boon_tech_artistic_desc.en: A grand opera house gives the arts a home and an audience. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_tech_artistic_desc.es: Un gran teatro de la ópera da a las artes un hogar y un público. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_tech_athletic_desc.en: A grand stadium makes a sporting people, and a healthier one. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_tech_athletic_desc.es: Un gran estadio forma un pueblo deportista y más sano. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_tech_industrial_desc.en: A great exhibition hall shows the best of the country's manufacturers to the world. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_tech_industrial_desc.es: Un gran pabellón de exposiciones muestra al mundo lo mejor de los fabricantes del país. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_tech_naturalist_desc.en: Botanical gardens turn the public's mind to clean air and water. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_tech_naturalist_desc.es: Los jardines botánicos orientan la mente del público hacia el aire y el agua limpios. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_tech_scientific_desc.en: A grand observatory draws scholars from abroad, and their ideas with them. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_tech_scientific_desc.es: Un gran observatorio atrae a estudiosos del extranjero, y con ellos sus ideas. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_boon_victory_desc.en: A monument to the victory keeps the triumph in the world's eye. Won from an opportunity.
gm_boon_victory_desc.es: Un monumento a la victoria mantiene el triunfo a la vista del mundo. Se logró gracias a una oportunidad.

gm_clear_landmark_line.en: #R A historical monument:#! its history goes with it.
gm_clear_landmark_line.es: #R Un monumento histórico:#! su historia desaparece con él.

gm_clear_req_full_tt.en: Six Grand Monuments stand in this state, counting a construction site
gm_clear_req_full_tt.es: Seis Grandes monumentos se alzan en este estado, contando una obra de construcción

gm_clear_req_least_tt.en: It is the least grand of them, contested ones aside
gm_clear_req_least_tt.es: Es el menos grandioso de ellos, sin contar los que están en disputa

gm_clear_req_quiet_tt.en: Nothing is under way here: no ceremony, naming, rebuilding or other order
gm_clear_req_quiet_tt.es: Aquí no hay nada en marcha: ni ceremonia, ni cambio de nombre, ni reconstrucción ni otra orden

gm_clear_tt.en: Clear it away to make room: it is gone for good, with its #v [THIS.ScriptValue('gm_state_primary_grandeur')|1]#! [concept_grandeur] and all it gave, and the grandest monument beside it takes its place. [SelectLocalization( EqualTo_CFixedPoint( THIS.ScriptValue('gm_disp_is_landmark'), '(CFixedPoint)1' ), 'gm_clear_landmark_line', 'te_tt_blank' )]\nSix Grand Monuments may stand in a state, a construction site among them; with one fewer, a new site can be started here.
gm_clear_tt.es: Despéjalo para hacer sitio: desaparece para siempre, con sus #v [THIS.ScriptValue('gm_state_primary_grandeur')|1]#! de [concept_grandeur|l] y todo lo que daba, y el monumento más grandioso que tiene al lado ocupa su lugar. [SelectLocalization( EqualTo_CFixedPoint( THIS.ScriptValue('gm_disp_is_landmark'), '(CFixedPoint)1' ), 'gm_clear_landmark_line', 'te_tt_blank' )]\nEn un estado pueden alzarse seis Grandes monumentos, incluida una obra de construcción; con uno menos, aquí se puede empezar una obra nueva.

gm_com_accept_build_line.en: The #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_target_levels')|0]#! levels its [concept_grandeur] takes at today's rate are queued at once in #v [SCOPE.sState('gm_com_build_state').GetNameNoFormatting]#! as government construction: #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_accept_cost')|0]#! construction.
gm_com_accept_build_line.es: Los #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_target_levels')|0]#! niveles que requiere su [concept_grandeur|l] a la tasa de hoy se ponen en cola de inmediato en #v [SCOPE.sState('gm_com_build_state').GetNameNoFormatting]#! como construcción gubernamental: #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_accept_cost')|0]#! de construcción.

gm_com_accept_head.en:
The opportunity opens: raise #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_target')|1]#! [concept_grandeur] in monuments dedicated #b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_dedication_name')]#! within #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_com_time_months')|0]#! months, in a new monument or one built beside another: a finished monument takes no more levels of its own, and years of age do not count.
Completed, it brings:
The monument that completes it gains #G +[SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_com_gift')|0]#! [concept_grandeur] at no cost.
The approval of the [SCOPE.gsInterestGroup('gm_com_ig_scope').GetName]: about #G +2#!, fading.
gm_com_accept_head.es:
Se abre la oportunidad: alcanza #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_com_target')|1]#! de [concept_grandeur|l] en monumentos con la dedicatoria #b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_dedication_name')]#! en un plazo de #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_com_time_months')|0]#! meses, ya sea en un monumento nuevo o en uno construido junto a otro: un monumento terminado no admite más niveles propios, y los años de antigüedad no cuentan.
Al completarla, aporta:
El monumento que la completa gana #G +[SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_com_gift')|0]#! de [concept_grandeur|l] sin coste alguno.
La aprobación de [SCOPE.gsInterestGroup('gm_com_ig_scope').GetName]: unos #G +2#!, que se desvanece.

gm_com_accept_hist_tt.en:
$gm_com_accept_head$
The monument that completes it becomes #b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_occasion_name')]#!, a historical monument with its own name and look.[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_hist_sig_line')]
This opportunity comes once: let it pass and it does not come again.
If time runs out, the moment passes at no cost.
gm_com_accept_hist_tt.es:
$gm_com_accept_head$
El monumento que la completa se convierte en #b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_occasion_name')]#!, un monumento histórico con nombre y aspecto propios.[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_hist_sig_line')]
Esta oportunidad se presenta una sola vez: si se deja pasar, no vuelve.
Si se agota el tiempo, el momento pasa sin coste alguno.

gm_com_accept_tt.en: $gm_com_accept_head$\n#b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_boon_name')]#! for #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_boon_years')|0]#! years: [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_boon_effect')].[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_special_line')]\nIf time runs out, the moment passes at no cost.
gm_com_accept_tt.es: $gm_com_accept_head$\n#b [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_boon_name')]#! durante #v [SCOPE.GetRootScope.ScriptValue('gm_disp_boon_years')|0]#! años: [ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_boon_effect')].[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_special_line')]\nSi se agota el tiempo, el momento pasa sin coste alguno.

gm_com_decline_tt.en: The moment passes. No one holds it against us, and the next moment can bring another opportunity.[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_special_pass_line')]
gm_com_decline_tt.es: El momento pasa. Nadie nos lo reprocha, y el siguiente momento puede traer otra oportunidad.[ROOT.GetCountry.GetCustom('gm_com_special_pass_line')]

gm_com_hist_sig_heroes.en: \nIts unique dedication, #b $gm_sig_heroes$#!: $gm_sig_heroes_effect$ for each step of its [concept_grandeur].
gm_com_hist_sig_heroes.es: \nSu dedicatoria única, #b $gm_sig_heroes$#!: $gm_sig_heroes_effect$ por cada escalón de su [concept_grandeur|l].

gm_com_hist_sig_liberty.en: \nIts unique dedication, #b $gm_sig_liberty$#!: $gm_sig_liberty_effect$ for each step of its [concept_grandeur], counted with every monument that carries it.
gm_com_hist_sig_liberty.es: \nSu dedicatoria única, #b $gm_sig_liberty$#!: $gm_sig_liberty_effect$ por cada escalón de su [concept_grandeur|l], contada con todos los monumentos que la llevan.

gm_com_hist_sig_martial_glory.en: \nIts unique dedication, #b $gm_sig_martial_glory$#!: $gm_sig_martial_glory_effect$ for each step of its [concept_grandeur], counted with every monument that carries it.
gm_com_hist_sig_martial_glory.es: \nSu dedicatoria única, #b $gm_sig_martial_glory$#!: $gm_sig_martial_glory_effect$ por cada escalón de su [concept_grandeur|l], contada con todos los monumentos que la llevan.

gm_com_let_pass_effect_tt.en: The opportunity closes at no cost, so the next moment can bring another.
gm_com_let_pass_effect_tt.es: La oportunidad se cierra sin coste alguno, de modo que el siguiente momento puede traer otra.

gm_com_named_space_moon_base.en: the first colony on the Moon
gm_com_named_space_moon_base.es: la primera colonia en la Luna

gm_com_raise_building_tt.es: Ninguno de nuestros Grandes monumentos está en construcción

gm_com_raise_effect_tt.en: The missing levels are queued as government construction. They count once they are finished and their monument is dedicated: its Dedicate button holds the ceremony, which offers the opportunity's dedication first.
